subject: literature
title: High Modernism (c. 1910–1930): the sentence breaks
dek: Woolf, Joyce, Eliot — and, in the same years, 新青年 and Lu Xun’s broken “I.”

thumb.alt: Virginia Woolf in profile, platinum-print portrait by George Charles Beresford, 1902.

hero.alt: Virginia Woolf in profile, 1902, photographed by George Charles Beresford.
hero.caption: Virginia Woolf (then Virginia Stephen), photographed by George Charles Beresford in 1902 — years before Mrs Dalloway. The face is earlier than the sentences this capsule is about. Beresford died in 1938; the portrait is in the public domain.
hero.credit: George Charles Beresford / Wikimedia Commons / public domain

honesty: “High modernism” is a later classroom name for a cluster of difficult, self-conscious works written mostly in English, French, and German around the 1910s–1920s. It was never a membership. This capsule uses the name, then looks at the same decades in Chinese vernacular writing — not as an appendix, as the same years.

timeline.label: The war
timeline.detail: European high modernism is unintelligible if you subtract the First World War.

timeline.label: 新青年
timeline.detail: Chen Duxiu founds Youth Magazine in Shanghai; it is renamed 新青年 the next year.

timeline.label: Two broken “I”s
timeline.detail: Lu Xun’s 狂人日記 in 新青年; Ulysses begins to appear in The Little Review.

timeline.label: The year of the pile
timeline.detail: Ulysses (book), The Waste Land, Jacob’s Room. A convenient classroom date, and a real cluster.

timeline.label: Woolf
timeline.detail: Mrs Dalloway; To the Lighthouse. Stream of consciousness as a method, not a mood.

glossary.explain: A way of writing that follows a mind’s associations rather than a plot summary. The phrase is older than Woolf; the method, in English, is often attached to her and to Joyce. It is a technique, not a personality type.
Low-circulation journals that printed work commercial houses would not: The Little Review, The Egoist, Blast, 新青年. Modernism’s distribution system was often a cheap periodical, not a first edition.
Vorticist magazine, two issues, 1914 and 1915, edited by Wyndham Lewis. The pink cover is easier to remember than the poems. It is one of the little magazines, not the movement’s bible.
T. S. Eliot’s 1922 poem, first in The Criterion and The Dial, then as a book with notes. Fragment, quotation, and a London that sounds like a ruin. Eliot later converted; the poem is not a sermon.

James Joyce’s novel of one Dublin day (16 June 1904), serialized from 1918, published as a book in Paris in 1922. The Little Review’s editors were convicted of obscenity in the U.S. in 1921 for printing it.

4 May 1919: Beijing student protests against the Versailles settlement and Chinese diplomats. In literary history the name also covers the wider New Culture years — vernacular writing, 新青年, a fight with classical prose.
Magazine founded by Chen Duxiu in Shanghai in 1915 as 青年杂志, renamed 新青年 in 1916. Democracy, science, vernacular literature. Lu Xun’s 狂人日記 appeared there in May 1918.
Lu Xun’s 1918 story: a first-person diary that reads Confucian virtue as cannibalism. Classical Chinese in the preface, vernacular in the diary. The broken “I” is the point.

aliases: The True Story of Ah Q
glossary.explain: Lu Xun’s 1921–22 serial. Ah Q, a village nobody who wins by telling himself he has won. Read as national allegory, as class comedy, and as a study of humiliation.
Writing in the spoken language rather than classical Chinese (文言). May Fourth writers treated 白話 as a political choice: who gets to read, and who the nation is imagined to be.
A third-person sentence that takes on a character’s diction without quotation marks. Woolf uses it constantly. It is one reason her “he” and “she” do not behave like a stable Victorian narrator.
African American literary and arts flowering in the 1920s, centered in Harlem. Contemporaneous with high modernism, not a footnote to it. Different magazines, different constraints, same decade.
Woolf’s 1925 novel: one June day in London, a party, a shell-shocked man. The war is inside the sentences, not only in the plot.

fun_fact.title: 1918, twice
fun_fact.text: In May 1918 Lu Xun’s 狂人日記 appeared in 新青年. That same year The Little Review in New York began serializing Joyce’s Ulysses. Two broken first persons, two little magazines, no transatlantic plot connecting them. The coincidence is chronological, which is enough.

blocks.text: Nineteenth-century realist and naturalist novels — in English, French, Russian — often trusted a narrator who could stand outside the scene and tell you what it meant. Even when the news was grim, the grammar was stable. Someone was in charge of the sentence.

That stability was already under pressure before 1914: interior monologue in Dostoevsky, Flaubert’s free indirect style, late James. High modernism does not invent inwardness. It breaks the sentence that used to carry it, and it does so after a war that made the old voice sound like a lie.

sections.title: Fragments, magazines, and more than one vernacular

blocks.text: The First World War is not background music. Eliot’s The Waste Land (1922) is a poem that cannot keep a single voice; quotation and ruin do the work a narrator used to do. Woolf’s Mrs Dalloway (1925) puts a shell-shocked man and a party on the same June day. Joyce’s Ulysses (serialized from 1918, book 1922) gives one Dublin day more interior traffic than a nineteenth-century decade.

blocks.alt: Pink-and-black cover of the first issue of Blast magazine, 1914, with the title in huge diagonal letters.
blocks.caption: Blast no. 1, 1914 — Wyndham Lewis’s Vorticist magazine, two issues and a war. Little magazines were modernism’s cheap distribution system. The cover is easier to remember than most of the poems inside.

blocks.alt: James Joyce in Zurich, photograph by Camille Ruf, about 1918.
blocks.caption: James Joyce in Zurich, about 1918 — the year Ulysses began to appear in The Little Review. The photograph was later used on a 1921 subscription form for the book, which is why it is public domain in the United States.
blocks.credit: Camille Ruf / Wikimedia Commons / public domain

blocks.text: Stream of consciousness is a method: follow the mind’s jump, do not tidy it for the drawing room. Free indirect style lets a third-person sentence wear a character’s clothes. Fragmentation after 1918 is not only a trick. It is a claim that the old continuous voice had been a luxury.

blocks.alt: Snapshot of T. S. Eliot in 1920, cropped from a photograph by Lady Ottoline Morrell.
blocks.caption: T. S. Eliot in 1920, from a snapshot by Lady Ottoline Morrell (d. 1938). Two years later The Waste Land. The snapshot is small and informal on purpose: this is not the later, public Eliot of the readings.
blocks.credit: Lady Ottoline Morrell / Wikimedia Commons / public domain

blocks.text: The same years, in Chinese. Chen Duxiu’s 新青年 (first 青年杂志, 1915) argued for vernacular 白話 against classical 文言 — who gets to read, and what a national literature is allowed to sound like. On 4 May 1919 students in Beijing protested the Versailles settlement; “May Fourth” later names both that day and the wider New Culture years. Lu Xun’s 狂人日記 (May 1918) puts a diary in the vernacular and a preface in classical, then lets the diary say that virtue is eating people. 阿Q正傳 (1921–22) makes a village nobody into a national problem. The broken “I” is not a London export. It is a contemporaneous solution to a different classical inheritance.

blocks.alt: A bound copy of 新青年 (La Jeunesse) displayed in a museum case, French title visible on the cover.
blocks.caption: A surviving copy of 新青年 / La Jeunesse, photographed in a museum case. The French subtitle is on the cover for a reason: the magazine argued in Chinese and looked, deliberately, toward Europe. Lu Xun’s 狂人日記 appeared in its pages in 1918.
blocks.credit: Photograph of a 1910s magazine / Wikimedia Commons / public domain

blocks.caption: Lu Xun, 1930 — after the stories this capsule is about, still the face later textbooks freeze. He died in 1936. Early photographs of him are in the public domain in China and, as tagged here, in the United States.

blocks.text: Also in the same decade, not in the same magazines: the Harlem Renaissance in the United States. Different constraints, different editors, a modernism that had to argue for the right to be modern. High modernism as an English-department brand is too small for 1922 if it can only hold Eliot.

sections.title: Three English names, one Chinese one

people.name: Virginia Woolf
people.caption: Beresford portrait, 1902.
people.text: Mrs Dalloway (1925), To the Lighthouse (1927), A Room of One’s Own (1929). The sentences move as a mind moves. The war is in the jumps, not only in the plot.

people.name: James Joyce
people.caption: Zurich, about 1918.
people.text: Dubliners, A Portrait, then Ulysses. Exile, serialization, a ban, a Paris book. The method is excess: more interior than a day should hold.

people.name: T. S. Eliot
people.caption: Snapshot, 1920.
people.text: American-born, London-settled. The Waste Land (1922) as the syllabus poem of fragmentation. Later he becomes a public Christian conservative. The poem and the later man are not required to agree.

people.name: Lu Xun 魯迅
people.caption: 1930 studio portrait.
people.text: 狂人日記 (1918), 阿Q正傳 (1921–22). Vernacular as a weapon against a classical prose that had pretended to be virtue. Same decades as Woolf and Joyce; a different broken “I.”

blocks.text: By the 1930s and 1940s a reaction is already audible: calls for plainer prose, political clarity, a novel that will do something. Mid-century English and American fiction often treats high modernism as a brilliant dead end. That verdict is a period style of its own.

Later postcolonial writers — in English and out of it — take the broken sentence and the unreliable “I” into other empires. They are not a delayed May Fourth or a delayed Woolf. They are what happens when the method leaves the original capitals.
If the narrator is no longer stable, who is the “we” in “we moderns”?
